problem.heading: An empty-looking home is the easiest target on the street.
problem.subheading: Dark windows, one lamp on a timer, silence in the hallway — that is what an opportunist checks in seconds, from the pavement. Kevin gives them the opposite: a home that looks and sounds lived-in, whether you are at work, on holiday, or the only one at home tonight.
problem.tile_1_body: Moving human silhouettes on the wall or ceiling, visible through the curtains — the sign of life a burglar looks for before choosing a house.
problem.tile_2_title: The sound of a normal evening
problem.tile_2_body: Conversation, a TV, cooking, a dog that barks at the doorbell — played from the device, so even up close someone is clearly home.
problem.tile_3_body: The same lamp at the same time every night reads as automation. Kevin varies light, shadow and sound for up to four weeks without repeating.
problem.tile_4_title: The layer your alarm doesn't have
problem.tile_4_body: An alarm reacts after the door is tested. Kevin works before: from the street the house looks occupied, so the attempt never starts. Keep your alarm — put prevention in front of it.

mechanism.heading: Light. Shadow. Sound.
mechanism.subheading: A burglar judges a home in seconds — by its light, its movement, its sound. Kevin delivers all three from one device, so your home looks lived-in from the street to the doorstep, and they move on to an easier target.
mechanism.phase_1_body: Warm light shifts like real lamps and a flickering TV — never the rigid on-off of a cheap timer.
mechanism.phase_2_body: Moving silhouettes pass behind the curtains — exactly what a burglar checks before choosing a target.
mechanism.phase_3_body: Voices, a TV, cooking and a dog at the doorbell play from the device — so even up close, someone is clearly home.

faq.a1: Kevin is a Swiss-engineered presence simulator. Placed by a window, it plays warm light, moving human shadows and everyday sounds from its own storage, so from the street your home looks and sounds lived-in while you are away — in flats, houses, offices and holiday homes.
faq.q2: How is it different from an alarm or a camera?
faq.a2: An alarm reacts after someone tests the door; a camera records what already happened and stops working when Wi-Fi is jammed. Kevin works before any of that: it makes your home look occupied so the attempt never starts. Keep your alarm — Kevin is the prevention layer in front of it.
faq.a3: No. Kevin has no camera and no microphone. It only projects light, shadow and sound. Simulations are stored on the device, not streamed from the cloud or shared with anyone.
faq.q4: What is included, and what does it cost to run?
faq.a4: One payment for the device, the app, 70+ hours of simulations and lifetime software updates. No monitoring subscription. Free shipping across the EU, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Iceland, 30-day returns and a 3-year Swiss warranty.
faq.q5: Does it keep working if Wi-Fi is jammed or down?
faq.a5: Yes. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are only used to set Kevin up and to install updates. Every simulation plays from the 32 GB inside the device, so light, shadow and sound continue even when burglars jam cameras and app alarms.
faq.a6: Galaxus tested Kevin.3 in January 2026 and called it “unrivalled in that it's an easy-to-use, all-in-one solution that delivers a truly spectacular show.” The effect is strongest where it matters: from outside, through curtains, at dusk. Placement tips are in the setup guide.

explorer.cover_title: Fits your home. Changes with your style.
explorer.cover_body: The magnetic fabric cover lifts off so you can change the colour without replacing KEVIN.
explorer.cover_detail: Choose grey or an optional Snow White, Forest Brown, Ocean Blue or Vulcan Red cover.
explorer.sound_title: Let your home sound lived in.
explorer.sound_body: Everyday sounds from behind the fabric help suggest someone is home, even when you are away.
explorer.sound_detail: When you are home, use KEVIN as a Bluetooth speaker for your own music.
explorer.controls_title: Simple control, right where you need it.
explorer.controls_body: Start or stop the presence simulation with the power button. No phone needed for basic offline use.
explorer.controls_detail: From standby, the middle button starts Bluetooth mode; the right button turns on the lamp. In those modes, the two right buttons adjust volume or brightness.
explorer.status_title: A useful signal. Smarter use of light.
explorer.status_body: The status light helps you recognise the current mode. KEVIN also has an ambient light sensor to help save energy.
explorer.status_detail: These two top openings are marked together. KEVIN has a status light and an ambient-light sensor; the published guide does not identify each opening individually. Blue status indicates Bluetooth mode. The sensor measures room brightness, not images.
explorer.light_title: Make an empty room feel occupied.
explorer.light_body: Changing light and moving shadows help create the impression of everyday activity inside your home.
explorer.light_detail: Place KEVIN 15–60 cm from a wall, with its effects visible from outside. This supports deterrence; it does not guarantee protection.
explorer.vents_title: Give KEVIN room to stay cool.
explorer.vents_body: The openings underneath let air reach the device for cooling during use.
explorer.vents_detail: Keep the vents clear. Place KEVIN on a firm surface, not soft fabric, and do not cover the device.
explorer.feet_title: A steadier place on your shelf.
explorer.feet_body: Four rubber feet help KEVIN grip a firm, level surface.
explorer.feet_detail: The feet raise the base slightly. Keep the space underneath clear so the ventilation openings stay unobstructed.
explorer.placement_0_body: Choose a room that can be seen from outside. A spot near a window or front door helps KEVIN’s light and everyday sounds suggest someone is home.
explorer.placement_0_detail: Choose the room with the best outside view, so the presence effect can be noticed.
explorer.placement_1_title: Give the light room to work.
explorer.placement_1_body: Place KEVIN 15–60 cm from a wall, with the rear lighting facing it. This gives the changing light and shadows a surface to play across.
explorer.placement_1_detail: Avoid placing KEVIN close to other lamps: their light can weaken the shadow effects.
explorer.placement_2_title: Keep it steady. Keep air moving.
explorer.placement_2_body: Use a firm, level surface. Keep the ventilation openings underneath clear so KEVIN can cool during use.
explorer.placement_2_detail: Do not place KEVIN on very soft fabric or cover the device. This guide explains placement; it does not guarantee protection.
explorer.tap_marker: Tap a glowing marker to discover a benefit.
explorer.bundle_added: Your selection is in the cart.
explorer.clusters_title: More variety. A more lived-in impression.
explorer.clusters_body: Single LEDs and vertical groups form the rear lighting array. Together, changing light and shadow help your home look occupied.
explorer.clusters_detail: The photos show single emitters and groups of three. Mitipi describes sequenced effect lights and background lighting; it does not publish a separate role for every LED in KEVIN.3.
explorer.reflectors_title: Light shaped to create an impression.
explorer.reflectors_body: The angled recesses guide the light rather than letting it spill evenly in every direction. This helps create distinct light and shadow effects.
explorer.reflectors_detail: Mitipi’s published design describes shaped channels that limit and direct light beams. This animation illustrates that principle, not a measured optical simulation.
explorer.bluetooth_title: Your music, when you are home.
explorer.bluetooth_body: From standby, press the middle button to use KEVIN as a Bluetooth speaker.
explorer.bluetooth_detail: A blue status light signals Bluetooth mode. Use the two right buttons for volume; press power to leave Bluetooth mode.
explorer.lamp_title: A useful light when you are home.
explorer.lamp_body: From standby, press the right button to use KEVIN as a lamp.
explorer.lamp_detail: The two right buttons adjust brightness. Press power to leave lamp mode.
